title: Elevation Finder: Height of Any Point
description: Find the elevation of any place with the Elevation Finder — click the map or search, read height in feet and metres from open terrain data. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, clicking the Colorado State Capitol steps in Denver returns about 5,280 feet — the surveyed mile-high mark — read straight from the terrain model.
quick_answer: The Elevation Finder reads the elevation of any point on Earth from open terrain data: click the map or search a place and get its height in feet and metres. Use it for trailheads, properties, summits and sites — the ground's own number, without a survey crew.

body.t: Terrain models sample the ground on a grid (about every 30 m for the global SRTM-based data) and average rooftops and trees to a degree — a click on a wooded slope can read a few metres off the surveyed spot height. Resolution, stated, is the honest limit.

faq: Where does the elevation come from?
Open global terrain models built largely on NASA's SRTM radar survey and its successors — the same data family most free elevation services serve.
They read about 0 m — the model is a land terrain model with the sea at sea level, which is the only honest answer for water.
The model is closer to ground than roof: radar-derived data partially includes structures and canopy, so dense city clicks can read a few metres high. For the dirt itself, surveyed data wins.

The base surveys are from the 2000s with ongoing refinements — terrain changes slowly except where humans move it (mines, reservoirs, new suburbs), and the model will not know about last year's earthworks.
